(1) document currency -- the 2016-filenamed PDF is accepted as the single official source of truth (no
second reward_terms link exists anywhere on the official site; misrepresentation there is SBI Cards' own
liability, not this ingestion's to second-guess). (2) the live page's 4-points=Re.1 statement-credit route

so this golden deliberately prices ONLY the catalogue-derived route (0.1882 Rs/point), not the better

reward/milestone/NACV numbers should be revisited -- they would rise materially (~+33%).
These expected values are Claude's own hand computation, cross-checked once against evaluate_card's own
output for arithmetic self-consistency (same discipline as CASHBACK/PRIME/OCTANE) and confirmed exactly
by `ingest publish`'s own golden gate (SS I.8) on 2026-09-05.
Normalise (uniform monthly split, all three amounts exact multiples of 12):
grocery: 300,000/12 = Rs.25,000/month. ecommerce (domestic): 750,000/12 = Rs.62,500/month.
ecommerce (international): 60,000/12 = Rs.5,000/month.
Eligibility (Stage 2): none of these three lines is fuel -- fuel_exclusion never matches this scenario.
All spend flows to reward, milestone, AND waiver views unchanged.
Match (Stage 3): grocery matches accelerated_10pt (priority 90, wins over base_2pt's priority 10).
Both ecommerce lines (domestic and international) match only base_2pt -- accelerated_10pt's selector
doesn't include ecommerce, and geography doesn't affect matching (no rule restricts on it).
Accrue (Stage 4), per_unit floor_per_txn, unit_amount=100 for both rules:
grocery: ticket_size=700 (registry default), floor(700/100)=7 units * 10 points/unit = 70 points per
Rs.700 -> rate = 70/700 = 0.1 exactly (zero rounding loss, 700 is a multiple of 100).
25,000/month * 0.1 = 2,500 points/month.
ecommerce (either geography): ticket_size=1800, floor(1800/100)=18 units * 2 points/unit = 36 points
per Rs.1800 -> rate = 36/1800 = 0.02 exactly (zero rounding loss, 1800 is a multiple of 100).
Domestic: 62,500/month * 0.02 = 1,250 points/month. International: 5,000/month * 0.02 = 100 points/month.
No rounding_estimated flag on either rule.
Caps (Stage 5): cap_accelerated_monthly = 10,000 pts/calendar month, scope=rule (accelerated_10pt only).
Pooled per month = 2,500 (grocery is the ONLY accelerated category active this scenario, so the
multi-category guard never fires -- see checklist item 5). 2,500 < 10,000 -> never binds.
Annual points: grocery 2,500/mo * 12 = 30,000. ecommerce domestic 1,250/mo * 12 = 15,000.
ecommerce international 100/mo * 12 = 1,200.
TOTAL GROSS POINTS EARNED = 30,000 + 15,000 + 1,200 = 46,200 points/year.
Thresholds (Stage 6-7):
fee_waiver: basis=waiver_eligible_spend, window=anniversary_year, tier threshold_amount=1,000,000.
tier fires, payload=waive_fee(fee=annual). waiver_achieved = True.
milestone_bonus_points: basis=milestone_eligible_spend, window=anniversary_year, tier_mode=cumulative,
4 tiers (300k/400k/500k/800k). Pooled milestone-eligible spend = Rs.1,110,000 >= all four thresholds
-> ALL FOUR TIERS FIRE: tier1 grant_points(10,000) + tier2 grant_points(10,000) +
tier3 grant_points(15,000) + tier4 grant_points(15,000) = 50,000 milestone points.
(Cross-check: the live product page's own 'Up to 50,000 Bonus Reward Points worth Rs.12,500 every
year' matches this exactly at THAT page's own implied 0.25 ratio: 50,000*0.25=Rs.12,500 -- this
golden prices the same 50,000 points at THIS bundle's own 0.1882 ratio instead, see Valuation below.)

see bundle currencies[0].routes[0]._note, ESTIMATED not issuer-stated):
gross_reward_value = 46,200 points * 0.1882 = Rs.8,694.84.

year1_fee = (joining_fee=4999 + charged_annual=0) * 1.18 = 4999*1.18 = Rs.5,898.82.
